policies.sentence: Grades rest largely on in-person, proctored or paper, closed-book exams and quizzes.
The instructor minimizes unproctored code assessment and runs assignments in controlled environments.
Students must record their screen during quizzes.
The instructor reviews screen recordings as one way to see students' work.
The instructor may conduct random code interviews for all projects.
The instructor asks live questions to check students' understanding.
AI can solve nearly any exercise instantly, so submitted code no longer shows understanding.
The instructor reduces program weight and designs projects for humans with minimal AI.
The instructor grades projects on functionality and correctness.
Students whose test answer can be found on the internet receive a zero for the test.
Students must not use an IDE on exams and are restricted to a terminal editor.
Students do exercises in class on their own keyboard, and make-up sessions follow the same rules.
Every AI assistant is blocked on the classroom network.
Students must submit homework as scans of handwritten originals.
Students who lean too heavily on generative AI earn little credit.
Assessment values team-specific detail about how the team was impacted.
Students must demonstrate their progress to the teaching staff at the end of the assignment.
Students are graded on progress, learning outcomes and collaboration, not the product.
